title: Historic Events Timeline
description: Place major historic milestones in their correct chronological order.

share.title: Historic Events Timeline
share.description: Can you place these major historic events in the correct chronological order?

seo.title: Historic Events Timeline Quiz - World History Game
seo.description: Play a free online history timeline quiz. Guess the order of major historical events, from the printing press to the moon landing, and build a streak.

items.label: Foundation of Baghdad
items.subtitle: Baghdad, Abbasid Caliphate
items.description: Caliph Al-Mansur founds Baghdad, which becomes a hub of the Islamic Golden Age and the House of Wisdom.

items.label: Viking Raid on Lindisfarne
items.subtitle: Northumberland, England
items.description: Viking raiders sack the monastery of Lindisfarne, traditionally marked as the beginning of the Viking Age in Europe.

items.label: Coronation of Charlemagne
items.subtitle: Rome, Holy Roman Empire
items.description: Charlemagne is crowned Emperor of the Romans by Pope Leo III, establishing the Holy Roman Empire.

items.label: Schism of East and West
items.subtitle: Rome & Constantinople
items.description: The Christian Church splits into the Eastern Orthodox Church and the Roman Catholic Church.

items.label: Battle of Hastings
items.subtitle: East Sussex, England
items.description: William the Conqueror defeats Harold Godwinson, leading to the Norman conquest of England.

items.label: First Crusade Captures Jerusalem
items.subtitle: Jerusalem
items.description: European crusaders capture Jerusalem after a siege, establishing the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

items.label: Signing of the Magna Carta
items.subtitle: Runnymede, England
items.description: King John of England signs the Great Charter, establishing the principle that everyone, including the king, is subject to the law.

items.label: Black Death Arrives in Europe
items.subtitle: Messina, Sicily
items.description: Genoese ships arrive in Sicily carrying the bubonic plague, initiating a pandemic that wiped out up to 60% of Europe's population.

items.label: Signing of Treaty of Windsor
items.subtitle: Windsor, England
items.description: The alliance between England and Portugal is sealed, becoming the world's oldest active diplomatic alliance.

items.label: Joan of Arc Lifts Siege of Orléans
items.subtitle: Orléans, France
items.description: The teenage peasant girl leads French forces to break the English siege of Orléans during the Hundred Years' War.

items.label: Invention of the Printing Press
items.subtitle: Mainz, Germany
items.description: Johannes Gutenberg invents the movable-type printing press, sparking a European information revolution.

items.label: Fall of Constantinople
items.subtitle: Constantinople (Istanbul)
items.description: The Byzantine Empire ends as Sultan Mehmed II captures the city, establishing Ottoman dominance in the region.

items.label: Columbus Reaches the Americas
items.subtitle: Bahamas, Caribbean
items.description: Italian explorer Christopher Columbus makes landfall in the Caribbean, starting centuries of transatlantic contact.

items.label: The Last Supper Completed
items.subtitle: Milan, Italy
items.description: Leonardo da Vinci completes his famous mural painting in the convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie.

items.label: Vasco da Gama Reaches India
items.subtitle: Calicut, India
items.description: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama lands in Calicut, opening the first sea route from Europe to Asia.

items.label: Sistine Chapel Ceiling Completed
items.subtitle: Vatican City
items.description: Michelangelo unveils the completed ceiling frescoes, representing a high point of High Renaissance art.

items.label: Martin Luther Posts 95 Theses
items.subtitle: Wittenberg, Germany
items.description: Luther posts his propositions protesting clerical abuses, igniting the Protestant Reformation.

items.label: Magellan Expedition Completes Tour
items.subtitle: Spain
items.description: The ship Victoria returns to Spain, completing the first recorded circumnavigation of the Earth.

items.label: Henry VIII Breaks with Rome
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: The Act of Supremacy declares King Henry VIII the Supreme Head of the Church of England, separating from the Pope.

items.label: Elizabeth I Becomes Queen
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: Elizabeth Tudor ascends the throne, initiating the Elizabethan Era and a golden age of English culture.

items.label: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
items.subtitle: English Channel
items.description: England defeats King Philip II of Spain's fleet, halting Spain's invasion plans and shifting naval power.

items.label: Dutch East India Company Founded
items.subtitle: Amsterdam, Netherlands
items.description: The Dutch East India Company (VOC) is chartered, establishing the world's first publicly traded corporation.

items.label: Founding of Jamestown
items.subtitle: Virginia, North America
items.description: Jamestown is established as the first permanent English settlement in North America.

items.label: Galileo Publishes Starry Messenger
items.subtitle: Venice, Italy
items.description: Galileo publishes his observations made with a telescope, including Jupiter's moons, revolutionizing astronomy.

items.label: Shakespeare's First Folio Published
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: A collection of 36 of Shakespeare's plays is published, preserving plays like Macbeth and The Tempest.

items.label: Taj Mahal Completed
items.subtitle: Agra, India
items.description: Emperor Shah Jahan completes the white marble mausoleum built in memory of his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

items.label: Great Fire of London
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: A major conflagration sweeps through the city, destroying the medieval City of London inside the old Roman wall.

items.label: Newton Publishes Principia Mathematica
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: Isaac Newton lays the foundations of classical mechanics and the law of universal gravitation.

items.label: Peter the Great Becomes Sole Tsar
items.subtitle: Moscow, Russia
items.description: Peter the Great begins modernizing and westernizing Russia, making it a major European power.

items.label: Invention of the Steam Engine
items.subtitle: Staffordshire, England
items.description: Thomas Newcomen builds the first practical atmospheric steam engine, starting the industrial age.

items.label: Lisbon Earthquake and Tsunami
items.subtitle: Lisbon, Portugal
items.description: A massive earthquake, tsunami, and fire destroy Lisbon, raising major philosophical questions during the Enlightenment.

items.label: Invention of the Spinning Jenny
items.subtitle: Lancashire, England
items.description: James Hargreaves invents the spinning jenny, revolutionizing the textile industry and paving the way for the Industrial Revolution.

items.label: Boston Tea Party
items.subtitle: Boston, North America
items.description: American colonists dump chests of tea into Boston Harbor in protest against British taxation without representation.

items.label: US Declaration of Independence
items.subtitle: Philadelphia, USA
items.description: The Second Continental Congress adopts the document, declaring the thirteen American colonies free from British rule.

items.label: First Fleet Arrives in Botany Bay
items.subtitle: New South Wales, Australia
items.description: British ships arrive in Australia to establish the first European penal colony on the continent.

items.label: Storming of the Bastille
items.subtitle: Paris, France
items.description: Revolutionaries storm the royal fortress and prison, marking a pivotal moment of the French Revolution.

items.label: Smallpox Vaccine Discovered
items.subtitle: Gloucestershire, England
items.description: Edward Jenner inoculates a boy with cowpox to protect him from smallpox, creating the world's first vaccine.

items.label: Louisiana Purchase
items.subtitle: Paris, France / Washington D.C., USA
items.description: The United States purchases the Louisiana Territory from France for $15 million, doubling the size of the nation.

items.label: Coronation of Napoleon
items.subtitle: Notre-Dame, Paris
items.description: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor of the French, signaling the end of the French Republic.

items.label: Battle of Waterloo
items.subtitle: Waterloo, Belgium
items.description: Napoleon Bonaparte is decisively defeated by coalition forces led by the Duke of Wellington.

items.label: First Public Passenger Steam Railway
items.subtitle: County Durham, England
items.description: The world's first public railway to use steam locomotives opens to passengers and goods.

items.label: Queen Victoria Ascends Throne
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: Victoria becomes queen at age 18, beginning the Victorian Era of major industrial, cultural, and political change.

items.label: Invention of Photography
items.subtitle: Paris, France
items.description: Louis Daguerre publicly introduces his practical photographic process, the daguerreotype.

items.label: First Telegraph Message Sent
items.subtitle: Washington D.C. to Baltimore, USA
items.description: Samuel Morse sends the first official telegraph message: 'What hath God wrought?'

items.label: Publication of Communist Manifesto
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels publish their pamphlet describing the class struggle and theory of communism.

items.label: California Gold Rush Begins
items.subtitle: Coloma, California
items.description: Gold is discovered at Sutter's Mill, leading to a massive migration of over 300,000 people to California.

items.label: Darwin Publishes Origin of Species
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: Charles Darwin introduces the scientific theory of evolution through natural selection.

items.label: Assassination of Abraham Lincoln
items.subtitle: Ford's Theatre, Washington D.C.
items.description: Lincoln is shot by John Wilkes Booth, just days after the American Civil War ends.

items.label: Invention of the Telephone
items.subtitle: Boston, Massachusetts
items.description: Alexander Graham Bell makes the first successful telephone call to his assistant: 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.'

items.label: Edison Invents the Lightbulb
items.subtitle: Menlo Park, New Jersey
items.description: Thomas Edison invents a commercially viable incandescent light bulb, lighting up the modern world.

items.label: Krakatoa Volcanic Eruption
items.subtitle: Sunda Strait, Indonesia
items.description: The cataclysmic eruption of Krakatoa destroys over 70% of the island, creating one of the loudest sounds in history.

items.label: Discovery of X-Rays
items.subtitle: Würzburg, Germany
items.description: Wilhelm Röntgen discovers electromagnetic radiation in a wavelength range known as X-rays.

items.label: First Modern Olympic Games
items.subtitle: Athens, Greece
items.description: The Olympic Games are reborn in Athens, featuring athletes from 14 nations.

items.label: Wright Brothers' First Flight
items.subtitle: Kitty Hawk, North Carolina
items.description: Orville and Wilbur Wright make the first controlled, sustained flight of a powered aircraft.

items.label: Special Theory of Relativity Published
items.subtitle: Bern, Switzerland
items.description: Albert Einstein publishes his paper introducing the relationship between space, time, and relative motion.

items.label: Sinking of the Titanic
items.subtitle: North Atlantic Ocean
items.description: The British passenger liner sinks on her maiden voyage after striking an iceberg, claiming over 1,500 lives.

items.label: Assassination of Franz Ferdinand
items.subtitle: Sarajevo, Bosnia
items.description: The heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne is assassinated, triggering the outbreak of World War I.

items.label: Russian October Revolution
items.subtitle: Petrograd, Russia
items.description: The Bolsheviks led by Vladimir Lenin overthrow the Russian Government, establishing Soviet Russia.

items.label: Signing of the Treaty of Versailles
items.subtitle: Versailles, France
items.description: The peace treaty officially ending World War I is signed, imposing heavy penalties on Germany.

items.label: Discovery of Tutankhamun's Tomb
items.subtitle: Valley of the Kings, Egypt
items.description: Howard Carter discovers the intact tomb of Pharaoh Tutankhamun, sparking worldwide interest.

items.label: First Television Demonstration
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: John Logie Baird demonstrates the first working television system to members of the Royal Institution.

items.label: First Talkie Movie Released
items.subtitle: New York City, USA
items.description: The release of the first feature-length motion picture with synchronized speech (The Jazz Singer) ends the silent film era.

items.label: Fleming Discovers Penicillin
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: Alexander Fleming accidentally discovers the antibiotic properties of penicillin, transforming medicine.

items.label: Wall Street Crash
items.subtitle: New York City, USA
items.description: The stock market crashes on Black Tuesday, triggering the onset of the Great Depression.

items.label: Amelia Earhart Flies Atlantic Solo
items.subtitle: Newfoundland to Northern Ireland
items.description: Earhart becomes the first woman to fly nonstop and solo across the Atlantic Ocean.

items.label: Discovery of Nuclear Fission
items.subtitle: Berlin, Germany
items.description: Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann split the uranium atom, leading to the development of nuclear energy and weapons.

items.label: Invasion of Poland
items.subtitle: Poland
items.description: Nazi Germany invades Poland, prompting Britain and France to declare war and initiating World War II.

items.label: Attack on Pearl Harbor
items.subtitle: Hawaii, USA
items.description: Japan launches a surprise military strike on the US naval base at Pearl Harbor, bringing the US into World War II.

items.label: D-Day Landings in Normandy
items.subtitle: Normandy, France
items.description: Allied forces launch the largest amphibious invasion in history, turning the tide on the Western Front.

items.label: Atomic Bombings of Japan
items.subtitle: Hiroshima & Nagasaki, Japan
items.description: The United States drops atomic bombs on the Japanese cities, leading to the end of World War II.

items.label: Founding of the United Nations
items.subtitle: San Francisco, USA
items.description: The UN is officially established to prevent future world conflicts, replacing the League of Nations.

items.label: First Computer Completed
items.subtitle: Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
items.description: The Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer (ENIAC), the first general-purpose digital computer, is completed.

items.label: Indian Independence and Partition
items.subtitle: India & Pakistan
items.description: India gains independence from British rule, resulting in the partition of India and Pakistan.

items.label: First Human in Space
items.subtitle: Vostok 1, USSR
items.description: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in outer space, completing one orbit of Earth.

items.label: Assassination of JFK
items.subtitle: Dallas, Texas
items.description: The 35th President of the United States, John F. Kennedy, is shot and killed by Lee Harvey Oswald.

items.label: First Successful Heart Transplant
items.subtitle: Cape Town, South Africa
items.description: Christiaan Barnard performs the world's first human-to-human heart transplant on Louis Washkansky.

items.label: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
items.subtitle: Apollo 11, The Moon
items.description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin become the first humans to land on the Moon.

items.label: First Microprocessor Released
items.subtitle: Santa Clara, California
items.description: Intel introduces the first commercially available single-chip microprocessor (Intel 4004), enabling personal computers.

items.label: Nixon Resigns Due to Watergate
items.subtitle: Washington D.C., USA
items.description: Richard Nixon becomes the first and only US President to resign from office due to the Watergate cover-up.

items.label: Eradication of Smallpox Declared
items.subtitle: Geneva, Switzerland
items.description: The World Health Organization officially declares smallpox eradicated, the first disease eliminated by human effort.

items.label: Invention of the Compact Disc
items.subtitle: Japan & Germany
items.description: Sony and Philips release the compact disc (CD), launching the transition from analog to digital audio.

items.label: Chernobyl Nuclear Disaster
items.subtitle: Pripyat, Ukraine (USSR)
items.description: A reactor at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant explodes, causing the worst nuclear accident in history.

items.label: Fall of the Berlin Wall
items.subtitle: Berlin, Germany
items.description: The wall separating East and West Berlin is opened, paving the way for the end of the Cold War.

items.label: Release of the World Wide Web
items.subtitle: CERN, Switzerland
items.description: Tim Berners-Lee introduces the World Wide Web to the public, revolutionizing global communications.

items.label: Nelson Mandela Elected President
items.subtitle: Pretoria, South Africa
items.description: Mandela is inaugurated as South Africa's first Black president, ending the era of Apartheid.

items.label: First Cloned Mammal (Dolly)
items.subtitle: Midlothian, Scotland
items.description: Scientists successfully clone Dolly the Sheep, the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell.

items.label: September 11 Attacks
items.subtitle: New York & Washington D.C., USA
items.description: Al-Qaeda terrorists hijack passenger planes, destroying the World Trade Center towers and damaging the Pentagon.

items.label: Human Genome Project Completed
items.subtitle: USA / International
items.description: Scientists complete the mapping and sequencing of 99% of the human genome.

items.label: Launch of Facebook
items.subtitle: Harvard University, USA
items.description: Mark Zuckerberg launches TheFacebook, marking the beginning of the modern social media age.

items.label: First iPhone Released
items.subtitle: San Francisco, California
items.description: Steve Jobs unveils the first iPhone, ushering in the modern smartphone era.

items.label: Election of Barack Obama
items.subtitle: Washington D.C., USA
items.description: Obama is elected as the first African American President of the United States.

items.label: Tohoku Earthquake and Fukushima
items.subtitle: Tohoku, Japan
items.description: A magnitude 9.0 earthquake and tsunami trigger a major nuclear accident at the Fukushima Daiichi power plant.

items.label: Discovery of the Higgs Boson
items.subtitle: CERN, Switzerland
items.description: Physicists announce the discovery of the elusive subatomic particle, validating the Standard Model of physics.

items.label: First Image of a Black Hole
items.subtitle: Event Horizon Telescope
items.description: Scientists publish the first direct visual image of a black hole's shadow at the center of the Messier 87 galaxy.

items.label: COVID-19 Pandemic Declared
items.subtitle: Geneva, Switzerland
items.description: The World Health Organization officially declares the COVID-19 outbreak a global pandemic.

items.label: James Webb Space Telescope Launches
items.subtitle: French Guiana
items.description: The most powerful space telescope ever built launches to study the early universe.

items.label: Death of Queen Elizabeth II
items.subtitle: Balmoral Castle, Scotland
items.description: Queen Elizabeth II dies at age 96, ending the longest reign in British history (70 years).

items.label: Rise of Generative AI (ChatGPT)
items.subtitle: San Francisco, California
items.description: OpenAI releases ChatGPT to the public, sparking a massive global boom in artificial intelligence development.
